note: Storage Entities defines a bundleable content entity type 'storage' with config-entity bundles 'storage_type' (config prefix storage.storage_type.<id>). storage_type config_export keys: id, label, description, help, new_revision, revision_expose, revision_log, name_pattern, status, has_canonical. Storage types are managed at /admin/structure/storage_types, entities at /admin/content/storage (a provided view) and created at /storage/add. By default there is no canonical URL unless has_canonical is TRUE. name_pattern auto-generates the entity name from tokens (e.g. [storage:string-representation]). Per-bundle permissions are generated by StoragePermissions. The optional rh_storage submodule adds Rabbit Hole behaviour. medium cases create namespaced storage types (storage_known/storage_canon) and read the config back; hard cases create a storage type (storage_task) and a storage entity of a type (storage_item); cleanup deletes entities then types so the baseline (no storage types) is restored.

evals.prompt: What is the Drupal 'storage' (Storage Entities) module for, and where do I create the bundles (storage types) and manage the stored data?
evals.expected_output: It provides a bundleable content entity type 'storage' for fielded data that has no front-end URL (an alternative to a content type hidden with Rabbit Hole). Create bundles (storage types) at /admin/structure/storage_types and manage entities at /admin/content/storage (add at /storage/add).

evals.prompt: In the storage (Storage Entities) module, how can I have each storage entity's name generated automatically instead of typed in by hand? Which storage-type setting does this?
evals.expected_output: Set the storage type's name_pattern to a token pattern (e.g. [storage:string-representation]); it is applied on every save so you can hide the name field in Manage form display.

evals.prompt: By default, can you visit a storage entity at its own URL in the Drupal storage module, and which storage-type setting changes that?
evals.expected_output: By default storage entities have no canonical URL - visiting /storage/{id} redirects to the edit form. Enabling the storage type's has_canonical flag gives items a real canonical view URL (with appropriate view permissions).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a Storage type called 'storage_known'. Inspect its live configuration and state the name pattern it uses to auto-generate storage entity names.
evals.expected_output: storage_known's name_pattern is [storage:string-representation]. Read it with `drush config:get storage.storage_type.storage_known name_pattern`.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, one Storage type is configured so its entities can be viewed directly at their own URL (/storage/{id}). Inspect the storage type configuration and name that storage type.
evals.expected_output: The storage type is 'storage_canon', which has has_canonical set to true (storage.storage_type.storage_canon:has_canonical = true).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use the Storage Entities module to create a new storage type (bundle) with the machine name 'storage_task'. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create a storage_type config entity with id 'storage_task' (e.g. \Drupal\storage\Entity\StorageType::create(['id'=>'storage_task','label'=>'Storage Task'])->save(), or via /admin/structure/storage_types/add).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a storage type with machine name 'storage_item'. Create a new Storage entity of that type whose name contains the word 'Eval'. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create and save a 'storage' entity of bundle storage_item with a name containing 'Eval', e.g. \Drupal::entityTypeManager()->getStorage('storage')->create(['type'=>'storage_item','name'=>'Eval Item'])->save().
